note: Wooded primitive camping area on a gravel pull-off lane beside Ben Branch Lake Trail, north of the 39-acre lake, with a privy; MDC calls it a 12-vehicle pull-off camping area. The lake is about 200 m south through the woods. Spot length is not published. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Individual Campsites' = one 12-vehicle pull-off camping area; the 8 GIS camping points all sit within ~200 m on one gravel lane (one cluster, no split). Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit; privy added. Pin is on the lane. Not waterfront confirmed. Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: area page: 'Facilities on the lake include a (12-vehicle) pull-off camping area'; map shows the primitive-camping and privy symbols on Ben Branch Lake Trail north of the lake. GIS layer 27 has 8 points (7 'Primitive Camping Area', 1 'Designated Camping Area') from 38.5740,-91.7887 to 38.5722,-91.7890, all on a gravel side lane (one-way loop off the main gravel road) within ~200 m of each other - one cluster, no split. Imagery: graded gravel lane with pull-off clearings under oak woods, reached on CR 314 and the area's gravel road; no ford, no posted limit. Spot length not published - pull-offs look car-plus-trailer sized, so a 23-ft rig should fit but it is unpublished (caveat kept in the note).
PIN: stored 38.57401,-91.78844 is GIS point 625 at the north end of the camping lane - fine (centroid of the 8 points is ~38.5730,-91.7887, ~110 m south; either is on the lane).
WATERFRONT: not waterfront confirmed - the southernmost spot is ~190-200 m from the lake's north arm through woods.
PHONE: (573) 815-7900 on the area page matches the stored phone.
Note rewritten: generic MDC text, the 14-day line (field holds it) and the directions dropped; '8 camping spots across the area' corrected to one lane.
